principles.md: Work through design trade-offs from local code structure to failure and change. Try each principle against a system you already know.
principles/simplicity.md: Trace a change through the call path and see which abstractions earn their place.
principles/single-responsibility.md: Draw boundaries around decisions that have different owners and reasons to change.
principles/least-knowledge.md: Give callers the result they need without exposing a collaborator’s internal graph.
Choose between a subtype contract and independently composed behaviors.
principles/make-invalid-states-impossibl: Use types to carry checked invariants from the input boundary into domain code.
principles/locality-of-reference.md: Compare the costs of scattered memory access, feature code and UI state reads.
principles/progressive-disclosure.md: Give common callers a short path and introduce configuration as their needs grow.
principles/prefer-deletion.md: Identify unused code and verify which installed versions and settings still reach it.
principles/design-for-failure.md: Decide how each failed dependency affects the screen, the saved data and recovery.
principles/determinism.md: Make the inputs to a decision explicit so a test can replay the same outcome.
principles/optimize-for-change.md: Invest in compatibility and recovery where an architectural decision is hard to reverse.
